subject: science
chapter_title: The World of Metals and Non-metals

concepts.title: Properties of Metals
concepts.definition: Metals share a family of properties: they shine when freshly cut or polished, can be beaten into sheets, drawn into wires, ring when struck, conduct heat and electricity well, and are heavy for their size.
concepts.key_idea: Lustre, malleability, ductility, sonority and conduction together identify a metal.

concepts.title: The World of Metals and Non-metals
concepts.definition: Materials divide into metals like iron, copper and aluminium, and non-metals like sulfur, carbon and oxygen; the ironsmith's tawa, bucket and tongs show how everyday tools are chosen from these two worlds.
concepts.key_idea: Two great families of elements: their contrasting properties decide what each is used for.

concepts.title: Rusting: Iron Meets Air and Water
concepts.section: Effect of air and water on iron
concepts.definition: A damp iron pan left outdoors turns brown and flaky: rust forms when iron meets both air and water, and the process eats the metal away, which painting and greasing try to prevent.
concepts.key_idea: Rust needs two partners, oxygen and moisture: removing either protects the iron.

concepts.title: Substances that Behave Differently and Uses of Non-metals
concepts.definition: Not everything follows the metal script: sulfur is brittle and dull, graphite conducts despite being a non-metal, and non-metals stay essential, oxygen for breathing, nitrogen for plants, carbon for all life.
concepts.key_idea: Rules have exceptions: the misfits teach us that properties, not labels, decide behaviour.
